body:
> Found reviewing #237 (PR #240) on 2026-09-01, immediately after `hkb edit` shipped. The card's goal was met;
> this is outside it.

## Why

`hkb edit` is the write half of the kb block, and two of its four flags take unvalidated input
(`src/cli.js`, the `edit` case):

```js
if (flags.priority !== undefined) fields.priority = Number(flags.priority);
if (flags['scheduled-at'] !== undefined) fields.scheduled_at = str(flags['scheduled-at']);
```

`hkb edit 5 --priority abc` computes `Number('abc')` → `NaN`, and `JSON.stringify` writes
`"priority": null`. The card's priority is **silently reset** — and the command reports `#5 kb: priority set`,
which is worse than saying nothing. The same shape applies to `--scheduled-at`: any string is accepted, and a
malformed one lands in the block where `computeReady` will parse it as an invalid `Date` and treat the card as
not scheduled, with nothing anywhere saying the value was junk.

Both are exactly what value 5 forbids: never a silent failure, and every error says what to do next. They are
also more dangerous here than in most verbs, because `hkb edit` is the command `hkb groom`'s findings tell a
human to run — including `priority_inversion`, whose whole purpose is to *correct* a priority.

## What

- **`--priority` must be an integer.** Reject anything else with exit 2 naming the flag, what was given, and the
  band (`0` unfiled · `1` normal · `2` next up · `3` urgent — #207). `Number.isInteger` after an explicit parse;
  do not silently floor a float either.
- **`--scheduled-at` must be a valid ISO instant.** Reject anything `new Date(...)` cannot parse, with exit 2
  naming the flag and showing the expected shape. Consider warning (not refusing) on a timestamp in the past,
  since a past `scheduled_at` is a no-op the card's author probably did not intend.
- **Validate before writing anything**, and for `hkb edit <n>...` with several numbers, validate the flags once
  up front so a bad flag cannot edit the first card and then fail on the second.
- Keep the decision pure in `src/model.js` so the parse is unit-tested without a board, per the layout rule.
- While here: `--paths` and `--goal` accept the empty string, which is a legitimate way to clear a field. Decide
  whether that is intended and say so in the usage line either way — today it is neither documented nor refused.

## Done when

- [ ] `hkb edit <n> --priority abc` exits 2 naming the flag and the band, and writes nothing.
- [ ] `hkb edit <n> --scheduled-at nonsense` exits 2 naming the flag and the expected shape, and writes nothing.
- [ ] A multi-number `hkb edit` validates its flags before touching the first card, covered by a test.
- [ ] The usage line says what clearing a field looks like.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass.
goal: hkb edit rejects a non-integer --priority and an unparseable --scheduled-at with exit 2 naming the flag and the expected shape, writes nothing when it refuses, validates flags once before touching the first of several cards, and documents how to clear a field
title: hkb edit accepts a non-numeric priority and writes null, silently resetting the card while reporting success
